title: Optimize Nested Loops and Repeated Calculations
content: Avoid quadratic O(N^2) nested loops by hoisting invariant computations out of loops, pre-calculating constant values, and leveraging set or dictionary lookups for O(1) membership tests.

title: Use NumPy Vectorization Over Python Loops
content: Replace explicit Python for-loops over arrays with NumPy vectorized operations or SciPy routines. Vectorized operations run in compiled C code and utilize CPU SIMD instructions to dramatically reduce CPU cycles and energy.

title: Cache Expensive Function Results
content: Use functools.lru_cache or functools.cache for deterministic or pure functions with expensive computations. Caching eliminates redundant CPU work across repetitive execution paths.

title: Use Generators for Large Data Streams
content: Prefer Python generator expressions and yield keywords over list comprehensions when processing large datasets. Generators compute elements lazily on-demand, minimizing RAM footprint and cache thrashing.

title: Stream Large File I/O in Chunks
content: Process large files line-by-line or in fixed-size chunk buffers instead of loading entire file contents into memory with file.read(), preventing high peak memory usage and swap overhead.

title: Batch Database Operations and Bulk Writes
content: Combine multiple individual database row inserts or API requests into single bulk/batch queries (e.g. executemany or bulk_create). Batching reduces network round-trip latency and CPU context switching.

title: Select Specific Columns in Database Queries
content: Avoid SELECT * in SQL queries; specify only the columns required by your application logic. Fetching fewer bytes over the wire conserves database CPU, memory, and network transmission energy.

title: Efficient String Concatenation
content: Avoid using the '+' operator in loops for string concatenation as strings are immutable in Python and cause repetitive memory reallocations. Accumulate strings in a list and call ''.join(list) or use io.StringIO.

title: Short-Circuit Evaluation with Generators
content: Use any() and all() with generator expressions rather than building full lists. Short-circuiting halts evaluation as soon as the truth condition is determined, saving computational steps.

title: Fast Membership Testing with Sets and Dicts
content: Convert lists to sets or dicts for repeated 'in' membership testing. Searching a list is O(N) linear time, whereas hash-based sets perform lookups in average O(1) constant time.

title: Compile Regular Expressions Once
content: Compile regex patterns using re.compile() at module scope rather than invoking re.search() or re.match() repeatedly inside tight loops, eliminating re-parsing overhead.

title: Avoid iterrows() in Pandas
content: Never use DataFrame.iterrows() for row-by-row iteration in Pandas. Use vectorized Series operations, DataFrame.apply(), or NumPy arrays for orders-of-magnitude faster and more energy-efficient execution.

title: Lazy String Interpolation in Logging
content: Pass log message arguments as lazy parameters (logger.debug('Value %s', val)) instead of pre-formatting with f-strings or '%'. This skips string formatting entirely when the log level is disabled.

title: Efficient Binary Serialization
content: Use high-performance binary formats like PyArrow, Feather, MessagePack, or Protocol Buffers for large structured data interchange instead of verbose text JSON or XML.

title: Reuse HTTP Connections with Requests Sessions
content: Reuse TCP and TLS connection pools across outbound HTTP requests using requests.Session() or httpx.Client(), eliminating repeated socket handshakes and certificate validations.

title: Reorder Conditional Logic for Early Failure
content: Order Boolean expression operands so that lightweight, cheap checks (e.g., integer equality) evaluate before expensive function calls or disk/network checks.

title: Use Local Variables in Hot Loops
content: Assign global functions or module attributes to local variables inside hot loops (e.g. append = my_list.append). Local variable lookups in Python bytecode are faster than global or attribute resolution.

title: Resource Cleanup with Context Managers
content: Always use 'with' statements for files, sockets, and locks to ensure resources are released immediately after use, preventing file descriptor leaks and system resource degradation.

title: Compress Large Network Payloads
content: Enable GZIP or Brotli compression for large network payloads to minimize data transfer size, conserving network bandwidth and reduce energy usage across routers and switches.

title: Asynchronous Non-Blocking I/O
content: Use asyncio or async HTTP/DB drivers for I/O-bound tasks to allow a single CPU thread to serve concurrent operations without wasting CPU cycles blocked in thread sleep or wait states.
